title: Transcriptomic-like EM cell types do not remove the 4- to 7-fold excess of EM inhibition between interneurons over slice recordings in mouse V1 (MICrONS v1507, Allen Synaptic Physiology)
abstract: Question: earlier work found that mouse V1 slice recordings detect only 9 to 74 percent of the inhibitory connections onto interneurons that MICrONS electron microscopy (EM) predicts at matched distance, and it listed a mismatch between EM target-based groups and Cre classes as an open cause. We tested this cause. Data: MICrONS v1507 (322 proofread inhibitory axons, 3.3 times more than before; metamodel types BC, MC, BPC as Pvalb-, Sst- and Vip-like for sources and for all 7,856 typed interneuron targets within 250 um) and Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 (21,958 probed V1 pairs). Method: ratio R of slice connections to EM-expected connections, matched by distance and layer, with a two-level bootstrap; tests written before the comparison. Results: 26 percent of proofread basket cells fall in the Sst-like group of the earlier rules. Metamodel labels raised R, but R stayed at 0.24 (95% CI 0.14-0.35) for Pvalb-Sst, 0.18 (0.13-0.23) for Sst-Sst, 0.16 (0.06-0.31) for Vip-Pvalb and 0.14 (0.07-0.22) for Vip-Vip; layer matching gave the same. Excitatory inputs to the same targets had R 1.1 to 1.5. The most favourable layer-preserving relabelling of EM types still gave R 0.25 (Vip-Vip) to 0.76. Only 0 to 8 percent of source axons had rates at or below the slice rate, and a zero-inflated target model permits at most 12.5 to 40 percent of targets without input against 76 to 86 percent needed. Slice and EM rates had the same rank order (rho 0.83) but slice rates varied 18-fold and EM rates 3.2-fold. A single per-synapse detection probability did not fit the nine pairs (p < 1e-50). Conclusion: class labels, layers, subpopulations and synapse number do not explain the deficit; functional silence of specific class pairs, pair-specific EM false positives, or animal differences remain. Limitations: one EM mouse, predicted (not Cre) types, unproofread target dendrites, post hoc models.

display.caption: A: slice/EM connection-rate ratio R (log scale, 95% bootstrap CI) for each class pair under five EM class definitions: the earlier publication (blue circles), its rules on v1507 (orange squares), metamodel types with the same proofread targets (green diamonds), metamodel types with all typed targets (yellow triangles) and with layer matching (purple triangles). Black bars: R under the most favourable layer-preserving relabelling of EM types. Dotted line: pre-set criterion 0.5. B: metamodel type against target-based group for the 322 proofread inhibitory axons.

A: distance-matched EM connection rate of each proofread source axon onto each interneuron class (dots) and the slice connection rate (black bar); numbers give the percent of axons at or below the slice rate. B: fitted fraction of EM target cells with no input (blue, 95% profile interval) and the fraction that the slice data need (orange).

A: slice against EM connection rate (log-log) for inhibitory-to-interneuron (blue), inhibitory-to-excitatory (orange) and excitatory-to-interneuron (green) class pairs; solid line equality, dotted line half. B: fitted per-synapse detection probability q of a synapse-multiplicity model with 95% bootstrap intervals; the dotted line is the rejected common q for the nine inhibitory-to-interneuron pairs.
